martyrdom: Beheaded by Herod Agrippa I in Jerusalem, c. AD 44

en.name: James the Greater
en.summary: Son of Zebedee and brother of John, one of the inner circle of three apostles closest to Jesus.
en.body: James, son of Zebedee, was a fisherman called alongside his brother John; the two were nicknamed "Boanerges" ("sons of thunder") by Jesus. With Peter and John he formed an inner circle present at the Transfiguration and the Agony in the Garden. The Acts of the Apostles records that he was the first apostle to be martyred, beheaded on the order of Herod Agrippa I around AD 44. Tradition holds his remains were later brought to Spain, where the cathedral of Santiago de Compostela became one of Christendom's greatest pilgrimage sites.
